---
title: "TROP implementations compared: the paper, Python, Stata and R"
description: >
  How the TROP paper, the official Python package, the official Stata command
  and cfcompare handle the main implementation choices, and how that has
  changed across releases.
---

The Triply RObust Panel (TROP) estimator of
[Athey, Imbens, Qu and Viviano (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.70061) is
available in four places:

- **The paper**, which defines the estimator, its weights and its
  leave-one-out cross-validation.
- **Python**: the official [`trop`](https://pypi.org/project/trop/) package
  ([zhaonanq/TROP-Estimator](https://github.com/zhaonanq/TROP-Estimator)).
- **Stata**: the official `trop` command
  ([justinwaddy/TROP](https://github.com/justinwaddy/TROP)).
- **R**: this package, `cfcompare`, an independent implementation that is not
  affiliated with the authors of the paper.

The implementations make different choices where the paper leaves room (how
weights are anchored when many cells are treated, how penalties are
cross-validated, how inference is done), and those choices change between
releases. This page records them as **dated snapshots**: each table describes
the four implementations as they stood at that date, and older snapshots are
kept unchanged so that the evolution stays visible. Jump to the
[latest snapshot](#as-of-october-2026).

## As of July 2026

Python `trop` v0.1.9, Stata `trop` v0.2.5, cfcompare 0.1.0.9006.

::: {.comparison-table}

|  | TROP Paper | Python | Stata | R (cfcompare)  |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Solver** | Silent | CVXPY using SCS or OSQP | FISTA (accelerated proximal gradient) | Soft-impute-style proximal gradient (base R only)|
| **Weight anchoring** | Per-cell  | Pooled only | Pooled (default) and per-cell (option) | Auto (choosing per-cell or pooled by treated-cell count) by default; per-cell and pooled as options |
| **CV criterion** | LOOCV | Placebo resampling (default) and k-fold (option) | Placebo resampling (default) and k-fold (option) for pooled; LOOCV for per-cell | LOOCV (default) and placebo resampling (option) |
| **Placebo pattern for staggered treatment** | N/A (LOOCV) | Common block | Actual per-unit patterns | Actual per-unit patterns; warning under LOOCV + staggered |
| **Outcome pre-processing** | Raw Y | Raw Y | Standardized (default) and raw Y (option) | Raw Y (default) and standardized (option) |
| **Covariates** | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| **Inference** | Bootstrap | None | Bootstrap | Bootstrap or jackknife (when available) |

:::

## What changed between July and October 2026

**Python `trop`**

- v0.1.10 (July 2026): Monte Carlo simulation tools that generate panels from
  features of a real dataset, to compare estimators; the estimator objective
  rewritten with `cvxpy.sum_squares`.
- v0.1.11 (September 2026): unit-level bootstrap inference, `trop.bootstrap`
  (controls-only resampling by default, or stratified). The repository moved to
  [zhaonanq/TROP-Estimator](https://github.com/zhaonanq/TROP-Estimator).

**Stata `trop`**

- v0.2.6 (August 2026): in the pooled `group(time)` mode, unit distances now
  mask the other treated units and the target periods; new
  `pooled_treat_distance(unit() time())` option to override a group's distance
  to itself.
- v0.2.7 (August 2026): adaptive cross-validation search, `vce(jackknife)`,
  progress bars.
- v0.2.8 (August 2026): the adaptive search starts with a sweep of the full
  grids.
- v0.2.9 (September 2026): in `group(time)`, the treated units are masked from
  the fit and the effect is estimated from the residual.

**cfcompare**

- 0.2.0 (October 2026): pooled anchoring per *treatment spell* (Stata's
  `group(time)` estimands, with per-spell effects in `fit$tau_groups`); pooled
  time weights centred on the spell midpoint; `pooled_treat_distance`;
  controls-only bootstrap resampling; delete-one-unit jackknife over every
  unit. See the [changelog](../news/index.html) for details.
- 0.2.1 (October 2026): this website; the comparison tables moved here from
  the README.

## As of October 2026

Python `trop` v0.1.11, Stata `trop` v0.2.9, cfcompare 0.2.1.

::: {.comparison-table}

|  | TROP Paper | Python (v0.1.11) | Stata (v0.2.9) | R (cfcompare 0.2.1) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Solver** | Silent | CVXPY (SCS for finite `lambda_nn`, OSQP for `lambda_nn = Inf`), `sum_squares` formulation | FISTA (accelerated proximal gradient with adaptive restart), warm-start nuclear path | Soft-impute-style proximal gradient (base R only; optional truncated SVD via `RSpectra`), warm-start nuclear path |
| **Estimands / weight anchoring** | Per-cell | Pooled only, over a single trailing block (`treated_periods`) | `group(time)` (default): one pooled estimand per *treatment spell* (same start and end, pooled across units), cell-weighted average; `group(cell)`: per-cell | Auto (per-cell when at most `max_cells` treated cells, else pooled) by default; `anchor = "per_cell"` or `"pooled"` (per treatment spell, as Stata's `group(time)`; per-spell effects in `fit$tau_groups`) |
| **Pooled unit distance** | N/A (per-cell eq. (3)) | RMS distance to the average treated path over the pre-periods | RMS distance to the group's average path over the periods in which no group member is treated; each comparison unit's own treated cells masked (v0.2.6) | Same as Stata; identical to Python on a block design |
| **Pooled time-weight centre** | N/A (per-cell `abs(t - s)`) | `T - tp/2` (half a period after the block midpoint) | Spell midpoint `(first + last)/2` (v0.2.4) | Spell midpoint by default; `trop_control(time_center = "python")` reproduces the Python convention, which `trop_matrix()` always uses |
| **Own-group distance** | N/A | Treated units compared with their own average (non-zero in general) | Same; `pooled_treat_distance(unit(#) time(#))` overrides the members' unit distance and the in-spell time distance (v0.2.6) | Same; `trop_control(pooled_treat_distance = list(unit =, time =))` |
| **Units with no usable comparison period** | Undefined (0/0) | Not applicable (block design: every unit shares the pre-periods) | Unit weight set to 0 when `lambda_unit > 0` (included when `lambda_unit = 0`) | Largest finite distance (smallest positive weight) |
| **Other treated cells in the fit** | Excluded | Excluded (block design) | Excluded; tau is the mean residual over the target cells (v0.2.9) | Excluded; tau is the mean residual over the target cells |
| **CV criterion** | LOOCV | Placebo resampling (default), k-fold; cycle, joint or adaptive search | Placebo resampling (default) or k-fold for `group(time)`; LOOCV for `group(cell)`; cycle, joint or adaptive search | LOOCV (default) or placebo resampling (`cv_method = "placebo"`); coordinate-descent (cycle) search |
| **Placebo pattern for staggered / general treatment** | N/A (LOOCV) | Common trailing block | Actual per-unit patterns, grouped by treatment spell | Actual per-unit patterns, grouped by treatment spell; warning under LOOCV + staggered |
| **Outcome pre-processing** | Raw Y | Raw Y | Standardized (always); lambdas on the standardized scale | Raw Y (default) and standardized (`standardize = TRUE`) |
| **Covariates** | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| **Bootstrap** | Stratified block bootstrap | `trop.bootstrap`: unit-level bootstrap, controls-only resampling (default) or stratified; percentile CI | `vce(bootstrap)`: stratified block bootstrap; percentile CI (no inference by default) | `se = "bootstrap"` (default): stratified (default) or controls-only (`boot_resample = "controls"`); percentile or normal CI |
| **Jackknife** | -- | -- | `vce(jackknife)`: delete-one-unit over every unit | `se = "jackknife"`: delete-one-unit over every unit (replicates that leave no treated unit are skipped) |

:::

## Numerical agreement with the official Python package

The TROP engine in cfcompare is written in base R. For correctness checks it
has been compared with the official Python `trop` package on exactly
comparable weighted-TWFE sample datasets, using `trop_control(svd = "full")`,
and the results agree to numerical tolerance. The matrix-in entry point
`trop_matrix()` keeps the Python package's signature and conventions for such
cross-checks.

## Notes on cfcompare's implementation choices

**Solver.** Finite nuclear-norm penalties are solved with a proximal-gradient
soft-impute routine, as opposed to FISTA or SCS, so that the implementation
depends only on base R; exact digits therefore need not match convex-solver
implementations. To reconcile the difference, fix the penalties via
`lambda = list(time =, unit =, nn =)` (bypassing cross-validation), set
`trop_control(svd = "full")`, and match the other implementation's anchoring.

**Cross-validation.** Penalties are chosen by leave-one-control-cell-out
prediction error by default (the paper's criterion); a placebo criterion that
resamples the actual treatment patterns is available via
`trop_control(cv_method = "placebo")`, and is the recommended choice under
staggered adoption.

**Per-cell or pooled anchoring.** `anchor = "per_cell"` solves a separate
locally weighted problem for each treated cell. `anchor = "pooled"` uses one
set of weights per *treatment spell group* -- treated cells with the same
start and end period, pooled across units, the `group(time)` estimands of the
Stata command -- and is faster. Under block adoption there is one group; under
staggered adoption one per cohort; a unit that switches in and out of
treatment contributes one group per spell. A group's unit distance is to the
average path of its units over the periods in which none of them is treated,
each comparison unit's own treated cells are masked, and the time weights are
centred on the spell midpoint. The per-group effects are returned in
`fit$tau_groups`, and the ATT is their cell-weighted average.
`trop_control(pooled_treat_distance = list(unit = 0, time = 0))` gives the
group's own units and periods the full weight (the Stata command's
`pooled_treat_distance()`). `trop_matrix()` is always pooled over a single
trailing block (the Python signature).

**Covariates.** Time-varying covariates can be supplied to `trop()` and
`panel_compare()`; they enter the low-rank term additively, as in Section 6.2
of the paper.

**Nuclear-norm floor.** For numerical stability, the solver adds a small
scale-relative floor to every finite `lambda_nn` by default (the reported
`lambda_nn` does not include it). `lambda_nn = Inf` (the DID/TWFE-like case) is
never affected, and `trop_control(nn_floor = 0)` applies the penalties exactly
as supplied.

**Standardization.** Estimation uses the raw outcome by default, so `lambda`
values are on the outcome's natural scale; `trop(standardize = TRUE)`
standardizes the outcome as the Stata command does, and then reports `lambda`
on the standardized scale.

**Inference.** `se = "bootstrap"` resamples units with replacement, keeping
each unit's full time series: treated and control units separately by default
(the stratified block bootstrap of the paper and of the Stata command), or only
the control units with `trop_control(boot_resample = "controls")` (the default
of the Python package's `trop.bootstrap`). `se = "jackknife"` deletes one unit
at a time over every unit, as the Stata command's `vce(jackknife)`; replicates
that leave no treated unit are skipped.
